LLM_description:
Subject: Network shipping plan to meet demand at the lowest total cost
Date: Today

Situation:
We operate multiple source locations supplying a broad set of destinations. Freight rates differ by lane, and available inventory varies across sources. Getting the allocation right drives transportation savings and preserves customer service levels. Partial shipments are allowed, which gives us flexibility to split deliveries across routes when it reduces cost or shortens lead times.

Problem:
We need a clear, lane-level shipping plan that allocates outbound quantities from each source to each destination. The plan must:
- Stay within the available inventory at each source
- Fulfill the required quantity at every destination
- Reflect route-specific shipping costs
Given that partial shipments are allowed, quantities can be divided among multiple sources and lanes to take advantage of lower-cost options while meeting service expectations.

Goal:
Identify the cheapest feasible shipping arrangement that meets all destination requirements without over-committing any source, achieving the lowest possible total shipping cost. The plan will be based on the attached supply, demand, and shipping cost data, and will be structured to support execution by our transportation and fulfillment teams.

LLM_description_template:
Subject: Most cost-effective shipping plan across our network
Date: [Insert Date]

Situation:
Transportation spend is a major component of our cost-to-serve. At the same time, dependable deliveries underpin customer satisfaction and revenue. We need a clear, efficient plan to move product from our warehouses and factories to our stores, customers, and regional hubs in a way that protects margins and sustains on-time, in-full performance without reliance on expediting.

Problem:
We must allocate available inventory from multiple source locations to fulfill confirmed requirements at multiple destination locations within the planning horizon. Each source has limited shippable inventory and handling capacity. Each destination has a defined quantity that must be received. Shipping costs differ by route due to distance, mode, and carrier rate structures. Partial shipments are allowed, so destination needs may be split across more than one source when that is more economical or improves service.

Our goal is to determine a shipping plan that:
- Does not exceed available inventory at any source
- Meets the required quantity at every destination
- Achieves the lowest possible total shipping cost across all routes

Next steps:
- Validate inputs (available inventory by source, required quantities by destination, and per-route shipping costs) and confirm any service or handling constraints with Operations and Carriers.
- Produce a lane-by-lane allocation that leverages partial shipments where beneficial, with clear instructions for origin-destination pairings.
- Review the plan for feasibility (dock schedules, carrier capacity, and transit times) and identify any exceptions or gaps requiring managerial action.
- Share the resulting shipping plan, projected freight spend, and key cost drivers with recommended mitigations.
